subject: Surveying and fitting around business operations
hook: Six things to agree before a fitter sets foot in your office
ig:
Six things to agree before a fitter sets foot in your office.

Fitting furniture in a business that's still trading is mostly about planning. These are the points we go through at survey so the day itself is quiet:

1. Working hours. When can the team be on site? Before opening, after close, a quiet weekday?
2. Noisy tasks. Wall fixing and drilling get scheduled away from customer-facing hours.
3. Access. Entrance, lift, stairs, loading bay and parking for unloading.
4. Services. Sockets, data points and floor boxes, so new desks and storage line up with them.
5. A named contact. One person who can make a call on the day.
6. Sign-off. How each area gets checked and handed back, so staff can move back in.

Agree these at the survey and the install becomes a plan rather than a disruption.

Save this for your next office, shop or clinic fit-out. Commercial enquiries via the link in bio.
fb:
Planning new furniture for an office, shop or clinic but can't really afford to close? You're not alone, and it's mostly a planning job.

When we survey a working business we go through: when the team can be on site, which tasks are noisy and need to happen out of hours, how we get in (entrance, lift, parking), where sockets and data points sit, and who on your side is the contact on the day. Getting those agreed early is what keeps the install calm.

on_asset: S1: Six things to agree before fitters arrive | Keep the business running | S2: Working hours on site — Agree when we can be in, and when we can't. Early starts, evenings or a closed day all change how the fit is planned. | S3: Noisy jobs scheduled — Drilling and fixing to walls are the loud parts. Booking them outside customer hours keeps phones and meetings usable. | S4: Access and parking — Which entrance, which lift, where the van can unload, and whether a loading bay needs booking with the building. | S5: Power and services — Where sockets, data points and any floor boxes are, so desks and cabinets line up with them rather than block them. | S6: Who's the contact — One named person on your side who can answer questions on the day and sign off each area. | S7: Save this for your next fit-out | Hours.
